_provenance.what: Verbatim claims from a REAL Google IAP assertion JWT, decoded from a live capture.
_provenance.how: e2e/okta/capture_assertion.mjs -- headless Okta sign-in (SAML) -> Workforce Identity Federation -> IAP -> gcr.io/google-containers/echoserver, which echoes the injected header.
_provenance.where: https://cru-iap-wif.matt-sandbox.ustech.app/ (project cru-iap-e2e-lb, org test.cru.org), federated to workforce pool keepzero-okta-poc.
_provenance.why: The offline integration suite mints synthetic payloads. This is the ground truth those are modelled on -- if Google ever changes the shape, the spec that compares the two will say so instead of the suite quietly testing a fiction.
_provenance.signature: Deliberately NOT stored. The signature is only valid for this exact payload and it expired 600s after capture, so it would be dead weight. Specs re-sign these claims with a locally minted key.
_provenance.identity: A throwaway Okta user at example.invalid -- not a real person, no mailbox.

notes: email is a BARE address -- no namespace prefix. The prefix appears on the sibling header, not the claim.
sub is opaque and useless as an identity. A sub fallback could never have worked here.
principal:// lives in the nested workforce_identity claim, NOT in sub. The verifier ignores it.
There is NO name claim. Callers seeding a display name must fall back to the email local part.
